memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
They put him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear
to them - Lev 24:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a small verse with a large lesson. The people did not know what
to do. So they waited.

They could easily have acted on instinct. The crowd was angry, the
offence was public, and mob justice would have felt satisfying. Instead
they held the man in custody and waited for God to make His will clear.

Dear friend, that restraint is remarkable, and it is rarely imitated. We
live in a world of instant reactions. Something happens, and within
minutes opinions are formed, messages are sent, and verdicts are
declared online. Waiting feels like weakness.

But Scripture praises it. James says everyone should be quick to listen,
slow to speak and slow to become angry (Jas 1:19). Proverbs says the one
who answers before listening brings shame on himself (Prov 18:13).

There is also honesty in this verse. They admitted they did not know.
How many mistakes could be avoided if we were willing to say, "I am not
sure yet — let me seek God on this"?

James promises that if any of us lacks wisdom, we should ask God, who
gives generously (Jas 1:5).

Before your next confident conclusion about a difficult situation, try
what Israel did here. Pause, pray, and wait for clarity.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I reacting quickly instead of seeking God's wisdom?
2. Am I willing to admit when I do not know?
3. What decision should I pause and pray over before acting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me the humility to say I do not know and the patience to wait
on You. Make me slow to speak and quick to seek Your wisdom. Amen.
